answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a juniper as the anchor of the cost.
